claim: Elasticity framework: output elasticity is decomposed into a probability channel and a capital channel, with a queueing multiplier only where near-capacity utilisation is evidenced.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Y = N x PoS (steady state). Probability channel eps_P = 10 x ((1-PoS)/PoS) x f x theta, with PoS=0.12 [E-3002] so (1-PoS)/PoS = 7.33; f = share of attrition attributable to the factor; theta = pass-through of a 10% factor improvement into that attrition class. Capital channel eps_C = 10 x c x tau x delta, with c = share of capitalised cost the factor touches, tau = fraction of that cost responsive to the improvement, delta = marginal-program quality discount (0.4-0.8). Time-only gains are credited to output ONLY through eps_C (fixed-budget program count) because a shorter step raises the steady-state approval rate only if it frees capital or capacity; a purely parallelisable speed-up produces a one-off level shift, not a rate change.

claim: B1 target validation elasticity is estimated at 5-15% per 10% improvement, point 10%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: eps_P = 10 x 7.33 x f x theta with f=0.45 (efficacy share of failures [E-3012]) and theta=0.15-0.45; = 4.9 to 14.8. Capital channel negligible. Point 9.9 rounded to 10. theta band reflects that a 10% reduction in the share of programs on non-translatable targets is not fully observable ex ante.

claim: B2 preclinical-to-clinical translation elasticity is estimated at 2-7% per 10% improvement, point 4%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: eps_P = 10 x 7.33 x f x theta with f=0.25 (portion of efficacy+tox attrition attributable to model non-predictivity rather than target choice) and theta=0.10-0.35 (bounded low because zero NAMs were fully qualified under ISTAND as of Jan 2026 [E-3015]); = 1.8 to 6.4. eps_C adds ~0.3 from reduced preclinical spend (c=0.10, tau=0.30, delta=0.6). Point 4.0.

claim: B3 recruitment and site capacity elasticity is estimated at 1.5-4.0% per 10% improvement, point 2.5%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: eps_C = 10 x c x tau x delta with c=0.30-0.40 (Phase III share of capitalised cost), tau=0.5-0.7 (time-proportional conduct cost at $55,716/day [E-3021]), delta=0.6; = 0.9 to 1.7. Add rescue of programs terminated for enrollment failure: probability of enrollment-driven program death rho=0.03-0.08, PoS_new/PoS_old ~ 1 + 0.1 x rho, contributing 0.3-0.8. Add a queueing multiplier of 1.3-1.6 because 48% of sites under-enrol or enrol nobody [E-3020] and >80% of trials miss the enrollment timeline. Total 1.5-4.0, point 2.5.

claim: B4 precision-medicine fragmentation elasticity is estimated at 0.5-2.5% per 10% reduction in screening burden, point 1.2%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Improvement defined as a 10% cut in samples screened per enrolled patient, holding enrichment constant. eps_C = 10 x c x tau x delta with c=0.15 (screening and prescreening share of trial cost in biomarker trials), tau=0.6, delta=0.6 = 0.5; plus schedule effect through B3 channel 0.3-2.0. Sign caution: reducing fragmentation itself (looser eligibility) would lower PoS via lost enrichment, so the elasticity is only positive when defined as screening efficiency.

claim: B5 regulatory review elasticity in the US is estimated at 0.1-1.0% per 10% improvement, point 0.4%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Review occupies roughly 10-12 months of a 9.1-year clinical development span [E-3004], so c is about 0.03 and tau about 0.5, giving eps_C = 10 x 0.03 x 0.5 x 0.6 = 0.09. Add up to 0.9 for evidence-standard effects (acceptance of NAM and biomarker evidence) which are more properly attributed to B2 and B15. FDA cleared 46-53 novel products in 2025 while meeting nearly all goal dates after losing 3,500 staff [E-3001, E-3029, E-3031], which is direct evidence of retained slack rather than binding queue.

claim: B6 manufacturing elasticity at whole-system level is 0.8-3.5% per 10% improvement, point 1.8%; for autologous cell therapy alone it is 15-40%, point 25%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: System level: cell and gene therapy is roughly 10-15% of clinical programs. Within that segment eps is high because utilisation evidence is unambiguous (only 60% of candidates secured a slot [E-3038]; 25% manufacturing failure in NHL [E-3034]) - a 10% throughput gain converts near one-for-one into treated patients and into avoided program deaths, giving 15-40%. Weighting 0.125 x 25 = 3.1, discounted by 0.4-0.6 because much of the CGT gain accrues to commercial supply rather than to approvals, giving 1.3-1.9; band widened to 0.8-3.5 for ADC conjugation and fill-finish tightness [E-3039]. Offsetting evidence: viral vector suite capacity is modelled to exceed demand through 2031 [E-3036], so the AAV constraint is cost and yield per dose, not suite count.

claim: B7 delivery elasticity is estimated at 1-6% per 10% improvement, point 3%, with an explicitly wide band.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Delivery acts by expanding the feasible target space rather than accelerating existing programs, so near-term eps_P is limited to programs already delivery-limited: f=0.15 of attrition, theta=0.10-0.40 gives 1.1 to 4.4. A long-run option-value term of up to 1.6 is added for indications currently outside the feasible set (CNS, solid tumour interior, muscle). The band is wide because no natural experiment relaxing delivery at scale has occurred; the ultrasound result [E-3043] is a 10-fold single-model gain, not a system observation.

claim: B8 toxicity and immunogenicity prediction elasticity is estimated at 3-9% per 10% improvement, point 6%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: eps_P = 10 x 7.33 x f x theta with f=0.30 (toxicity share of failures [E-3045]) and theta=0.15-0.40; = 3.3 to 8.8. Toxicity failures are additionally concentrated late, so avoided spend adds a small capital channel; and toxicity drives about two thirds of post-launch withdrawals [E-3047], which raises expected commercial value per approval. Point 6.0.

If raw-pool slack were the operative variable, cheap exhaustive screening would have converted it; it did not. I therefore withdraw the inference. The data I reported [E-3023, E-3024] stand; the reading of them does not. derivation: Agent D reproduced four of my point elasticities to within 0.35 percentage points WITHOUT the budget constraint: B1 +10.19 vs my 10.0, B2 +3.77 vs 4.0, B8 +5.66 vs 6.0, B10 +1.13 vs 1.0 [D report section 6]. That is independent confirmation of my arithmetic from different stage probabilities. With the industry R&D budget binding - D's default and the realistic case, since capital sits at utilisation 1.00 in every D scenario - each falls by about a third: B1 +7.05, B2 +2.65, B8 +3.96, B10 +0.80. I adopt D's budget-binding values as point estimates because the brief's output metric is annual approvals in the real system, and retain the unconstrained values as each band's upper bound. Implied scaling factor 7.05/10.19 = 0.69, 2.65/3.77 = 0.70, 3.96/5.66 = 0.70, 0.80/1.13 = 0.71; I apply 0.64-0.70 across the probability channel, taking the lower end where a candidate also loads the Phase III patient resource that D shows saturating.

claim: Duration and capacity levers are revised down hard: on D's model a 40% cut in enrollment duration and a 50% cut in CMC lead time each produce exactly zero additional annual approvals.

derivation: D scenarios S2, S3 and S4 all return 54.45 approvals; enrollment -40% and CMC lead time -50% change capitalized cost by -13.3% and -0.06% and change risk-adjusted cost not at all, because they shorten the carrying period without reducing out-of-pocket spend per programme [D report section 3]. D's tornado is consistent and adds an asymmetry I had missed: nearly every capacity parameter has a large DOWNSIDE swing and a zero UPSIDE swing - aseptic fill-finish -20% capacity costs 7.8% of approvals while +100% adds none; NHP toxicology capacity -30% costs 43% while +50% adds none; autologous cell-therapy suite capacity and mAb drug-substance capacity have zero swing in both directions. The reason is that capital binds first, so freed physical capacity has nothing to do. I therefore cut B3 from 2.5 to 0.6, B6 from 1.8 to 0.45, B16 from 2.0 to 1.4, B4 from 1.2 to 0.6 and B9 from 0.9 to 0.5. I do not cut them to zero, because D lists exogenous capital as an explicit model assumption with no feedback from returns onto budget, and in a real market a durable reduction in cost per approval does attract capital. B16 is cut least because it removes out-of-pocket procedures rather than only calendar time, which is the one channel D's own budget identity converts into approvals.

First, D's tornado: raising the industry R&D budget 50% above baseline yields zero additional approvals (50.0 to 50.0) because physical capacities take over the moment capital stops binding, while cutting it 20% costs 46% of approvals (50.0 to 26.9). The upside elasticity of capital is therefore near zero at the current margin and the downside elasticity is about 2.3. Second, X-10, partially adopted: aggregate capital is abundant at about USD 1.3 trillion deployable at the top 25 pharmaceutical companies [E-9526], and novel-target entry fell to about 30 per year in 2024 while venture investment tripled [E-9509] - the marginal dollar was available and declined the novel bet. The measured policy channel survives and is better identified than the industry-commissioned figure I originally carried: an interrupted time-series finds an immediate reduction of 11.4 industry-sponsored trials plus 1.2 per month after IRA passage [E-9525], which supersedes [E-3059] as the load-bearing estimate.
